## Household and background

Tobias Okonkwo (born January 27, 1994) is single with no dependents and rents unit 4 at 6 Kestrel Street. 2025 was a layoff year.

He taught fifth grade at the Fairhaven Consolidated School District until the district cut positions in July. His W-2 shows box 1 wages of $19,840.00 and $1,140.00 of federal withholding — and box 12 code E, $2,480.00 of elective deferrals into the district's §403(b) plan. (That deferral is why box 1 ($19,840) and boxes 3 and 5 ($22,320) differ: a deferral is out of box 1 but still inside FICA.)

From August he collected unemployment: Form 1099-G box 1 $11,260.00, with $1,126.00 withheld — he ticked the voluntary 10% box on the state's form, which is the reason he is not facing a bill now.

He also paid $1,742.00 of interest on his own student loans (Form 1098-E), spent $320.00 of his own money on classroom supplies before the layoff, and — on his sister's advice — put $2,000.00 into a traditional IRA in December to bring his income down.

## Interview

**Q.** Is the unemployment taxable? Most people have heard it isn't.

**A.** That's what I assumed — [Preparer: it is FULLY taxable on the federal return. The $10,200 exclusion people remember was a ONE-YEAR 2020 rule (ARPA) and does not exist for 2025.]

**Q.** Good news is you had them withhold 10%. Was that automatic?

**A.** No — there was a box on the claim form. I almost skipped it.

**Q.** The $320 of classroom supplies — was any of it reimbursed by the district?

**A.** None of it. That was out of my pocket.

**Q.** Did you deduct the student loan interest before, and do you know if you can, with the standard deduction?

**A.** I thought you had to itemize for it. [Preparer: no — student loan interest is an ABOVE-THE-LINE adjustment. He gets it AND the $15,750 standard deduction.]

**Q.** The IRA — traditional or Roth, and were you covered by a plan at work?

**A.** Traditional. And yes, the 403(b) at school. [Preparer: still fully deductible — the covered-by-a-plan phaseout for a single filer starts at $79,000 of MAGI and he is nowhere near it.]

**Q.** Did you take any money OUT of a retirement account in the last three years?

**A.** No, nothing.

**Q.** Any dependents, and could anyone claim you?

**A.** No to both — I've supported myself since college.
